name: Fungi
kicker: Kingdom of molds, yeasts, mushrooms · Decomposers with no chlorophyll
dates: Classified as its own kingdom in 1969
briefing: Mushrooms, molds, yeasts, and truffles might look like plants, but fungi actually form their own kingdom of life. Lacking chlorophyll, most fungi feed by decomposing dead matter or by forming partnerships with plant roots called mycorrhizae. Unlike a plant’s cellulose walls, a fungal cell wall is built from a tough material called chitin, the same substance found in insect shells.

tossups.p: A parasitic genus called cordyceps infects and eventually takes over the bodies of insects from the inside. Specialized coiled hyphae called pelotons form when some of these organisms trade nutrients with orchid roots, and a spore-bearing tissue layer called the hymenium lines the gills of many mushroom-forming species.
tossups.r: Cell walls in this kingdom are built from chitin rather than cellulose, and its members lack chlorophyll entirely. For 10 points, name this kingdom of decomposers and parasites that includes mushrooms, molds, and yeasts.

tossups.p: One kind discovered at the Chernobyl disaster site appears to convert radiation into usable energy. A toxic kind called ergot infects rye and once caused outbreaks of “St. Anthony’s Fire,” while another kind, prized in Mexican cooking, infects corn and is called corn smut.
tossups.r: Thread-like filaments called hyphae tangle together into a network called mycelium, and partnering with algae instead forms a lichen. For 10 points, name this kingdom that also includes mushrooms, molds, and yeasts.

tossups.p: Agaricus bisporus, sold in button and portobello forms, is one of the most widely farmed species in this kingdom, while the extremely poisonous “death cap” is a wild member of the same group. Some members transfer nuclei between adjoining cells through structures called clamp connections.
tossups.r: Many members partner with plant roots in a mutually beneficial relationship called mycorrhizae, trading nutrients for sugar. For 10 points, name this kingdom whose cell walls are made of chitin, not cellulose.

tossups.p: Truffles, dug up by trained dogs or pigs, are the underground fruiting bodies of one group within this kingdom. Spores form inside microscopic sacs called asci or on club-shaped structures called basidia, and a toxic kind called ergot once caused outbreaks of “St. Anthony’s Fire” in people who ate infected rye.
tossups.r: Lacking chlorophyll, members of this kingdom cannot make their own food and instead decompose dead matter or team up with plant roots. For 10 points, name this kingdom that includes mushrooms, molds, and yeasts.

trap.title: Fungi, or just a plant?
trap.body: Mushrooms and molds look plant-like and do not move, but they are not plants — they cannot make their own food, since they lack chlorophyll entirely. Their cell walls are also built differently: chitin here, versus cellulose in a true plant’s cell wall. A lichen, built from a fungus paired with algae, is a different combined organism, not this kingdom alone.
trap.fix: If clues mention chlorophyll, photosynthesis, or cellulose cell walls, that points to a plant or alga, not this kingdom. If clues mention chitin cell walls, hyphae, mycorrhizae, decomposing dead matter, or no chlorophyll at all, that points here.
trap.line: Real answer line: Fungi (accept fungus) [reject plants, algae].
